Document Title: AITG: Automating Intent-Oriented Task Generation for Mobile GUI-Agent
Authors: C. Zhang; Y. Huang; M. Tu
Author Affiliations: Samsung Research China, Beijing, China; National University of Singapore, Singapore; Samsung Research China, Beijing, China
Publication Title: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
Abstract: The advancement of large language models has significantly propelled research in mobile graphical user interface (GUI) agents, concurrently amplifying the demand for high-quality benchmark and data. However, existing benchmark data collection methodologies remain heavily reliant on manual effort, especially for designing high-quality queries for mobile GUI-agent. Furthermore, most benchmarks and training data for mobile GUI agent focus on English environments and lack localized application. To address these limitations, we propose an automated pipeline for generating intent-oriented tasks by selecting suitable task execution trajectories with Focus Score. This pipeline includes three phases, namely Seed Path selection, Focus Score extension, and Intent-oriented Query generation. It achieves automated data generation while ensuring the authenticity of the collected trajectories. Utilizing the generated dataset, we have evaluated and fine-tuned existing GUI agents. The experimental results demonstrate the practical utility of our automatically generated data for enhancing the performance of real-world models. 1.

Document Title: PWA: Process-Level Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
Authors: D. Fu; W. Hong; K. He; C. Wang; Z. Gongque; Y. Wang; W. Xu
Author Affiliations: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China; State Key Laboratory of Massive Personalized Customization System and Technology, China; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China
Publication Title: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities to interact with complex environments and autonomously complete tasks. In this paper, we propose PWA, a semi-online Process Reward Supervised Web Agent Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework. We investigate two key topics: 1) Constructing the process reward model (PRM) in a web agent scenario, and 2) Utilizing PRM in RL. For the first topic, we found that training a dense PRM is better than using MCTS or a prompted GPT-4. For the second topic, we designed a novel value-free RL algorithm that effectively incorporates PRM’s process signals during training. Our experiments, conducted on WebArena-Lite, demonstrate that this approach outperforms previous RL-based agents.
